answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency rule: each identity’s action profile is fingerprinted per epoch as a comet of session features (timing, task mix, counterpart graph), and continuity is enforced by requiring the next epoch’s fingerprint to fall within a tolerance band of its own history. A hollow match — near-zero drift, typical of cloned scripts — is rejected. Mismatches above the violet threshold trigger revalidation. Attackers pay by having to sustain distinct, drifting behaviour across every clone for many epochs, multiplying operational cost per identity.
